テキスト1 cha 145: Allow me to explain the references. A reference is, as I said at the outset, material for coming to know this world.
テキスト2 cha 130: It is not that you must necessarily check them, but if you wish to know this world more deeply, active viewing is recommended.
テキスト3 cha 150: Some of them are difficult and call for advanced knowledge, so if one concerns you, looking it up on the internet would be advisable.
テキスト4 cha 158: Conversely, some references are of no use whatsoever, so the power to judge whether one is needed is also called for.
テキスト5 cha 153: Yet it is not rare for something that looks of no use to be important information later on.
テキスト6 cha 152: In any case, if you wish to know this world deeply, checking every one without omission would be best.
テキスト7 cha 102: An unviewed reference carries a 'New!!' mark.

テキスト1 cha 145: To view a reference, please first select any reference on this screen.
テキスト2 cha 130: Holding the mouse pointer on a thumbnail displays a brief description at the bottom of the screen.
テキスト3 cha 150: Clicking a thumbnail then takes you into an individual summary screen like this one.
テキスト4 cha 158: Clicking the image in this summary begins the viewing of the reference.
テキスト5 cha 153: By clicking this arrow you may also move to the neighboring reference.
テキスト6 cha 152: It would be well to try it once for yourself first.

テキスト1 cha 145: References increase automatically, as a rule, as you advance through the scenarios.
テキスト2 cha 130: A reference notifier like this appears, and at that point it means the corresponding reference has been unlocked.
テキスト3 cha 150: Left-clicking this reference notifier while the text is waiting moves you to that reference at once.
テキスト4 cha 158: When you exit the reference, you can resume from where the scenario left off.
テキスト5 cha 153: However, some references seem not to be unlocked, or not to be viewable, unless a certain special condition is met.
テキスト6 cha 152: I am sorry, but as for references requiring special conditions, I too do not have a grasp of them.

テキスト1 cha 145: References are classified, as a rule, into two kinds: object and scenario.
テキスト2 cha 130: The object format comes in various kinds, such as documents, web pages and tangible things, but the operation is the same for all.
テキスト3 cha 150: In the scenario format a short story unfolds, almost the same as a scenario of the main work.
テキスト4 cha 158: There seem to be unknown formats among them as well, but, if I may presume, I do not have a grasp of those either.

テキスト1 cha 145: References are classified, as a rule, into two kinds: object, scenario, letters and report.
テキスト2 cha 130: The object format comes in various kinds, such as documents, web pages and tangible things, but the operation is the same for all.
テキスト3 cha 150: In the scenario format a short story unfolds, almost the same as a scenario of the main work.
テキスト4 cha 158: In the letters format you can view letters written long ago. However, you must spend points to read all of them.
テキスト5 cha 153: In the report format you can view reports written before the war. Here too, spending points widens the area you can read.

テキスト1 cha 145: In the object format there is often not only the displayed thing itself but a hidden comment embedded in it.
テキスト2 cha 130: In this way, holding the mouse pointer on a particular spot makes a mark appear, and that means it can be clicked.
テキスト3 cha 150: Clicking it displays what the viewer thought at that moment, so you may use it as still more detailed information.
テキスト4 cha 158: For the number of clickable spots, please refer to this 'Node'. A viewed node is marked with a check.

テキスト1 cha 145: The scenario format proceeds much as a scenario of the main work does, so you are unlikely to be at much of a loss.
テキスト2 cha 130: However, there are no save, load, reference or encyclopedia buttons.

テキスト1 cha 145: By using the filter you can narrow down the references that are displayed.
テキスト2 cha 130: As the references increase, choosing only the ones you want becomes hard. In such a case, please use this filtering function.
テキスト3 cha 150: On the reference selection screen there is a filter like this.
テキスト4 cha 158: A yellow marker sits at the upper left of each button; the lit ones are displayed. A left click toggles the light on or off.
テキスト5 cha 153: By kind: object, scenario, letters, other. By viewing status, three kinds: new (unread), broken off and complete.
テキスト6 cha 152: You may switch freely on the selection screen, so please try it out. There is no particular limit on use.

テキスト1 cha 145: I have not confirmed it myself, but it seems there are formats besides object and scenario that are categorized as higher.
テキスト2 cha 130: Their unlock conditions are strict, and broad knowledge seems to be required as well.
テキスト3 cha 150: I do not know whether /VAR/-sama should know this much, but if the chance arises, please look at them.

テキスト1 cha 145: The letters format consists of horizontally long letters; at first, almost all of each is hidden and cannot be read.
テキスト2 cha 130: As you keep clicking the letter, points are spent and the area you can read expands.
テキスト3 cha 150: However, please be aware that if your points run out, you cannot expand the readable area any further.
テキスト4 cha 158: Also, letters generally have many stains and cannot be read clearly.
テキスト5 cha 153: Once you can read the whole area, the stains disappear and clear letters emerge.
テキスト6 cha 152: For details, please refer to the help when you select a letter reference.

テキスト1 cha 145: The report format is a report from a certain organization, but most of it is missing and cannot be read properly.
テキスト2 cha 130: By spending points, it is possible to add the missing pieces.
テキスト3 cha 150: But, those pieces are scattered as in a puzzle, so you must return them to the proper positions with the mouse.
テキスト4 cha 158: Once all the pieces are fitted into their proper positions, the stains on the page disappear and clear letters emerge.
テキスト5 cha 153: For detailed instructions on handling the pieces, please refer to the help within the report screen.

テキスト1 cha 145: Have you noticed that there are points like these?
テキスト2 cha 130: These points are added by the main scenarios, by viewing references and by chatter.
テキスト3 cha 150: They are spent when you view certain references.

テキスト1 cha 145: Have you noticed that there are points like these?
テキスト2 cha 130: These points are added by the main scenarios, by viewing references and by chatter.
テキスト3 cha 150: In the letters and report formats, you must spend these points to expand the area that you can read.
テキスト4 cha 158: In the letters format, the more paper you pull away, the more your points decrease.
テキスト5 cha 153: In the report format, points are spent each time you add a piece.

テキスト1 cha 145: Very rarely there is a reference that cannot even be viewed unless a set condition is met.
テキスト2 cha 130: Even if it is unlocked, you cannot enter the viewing screen unless the condition is met.
テキスト3 cha 150: The condition for unlocking the lock is not announced, so I am afraid you must search it out yourself.
テキスト4 cha 158: The one thing I can say is that the lock is released by viewing other references.

テキスト1 cha 145: 'Reference' is an English word meaning 'reference material', and it is no more than something to consult.
テキスト2 cha 130: However, this is an extremely unstable world. There is no telling what may happen from viewing a reference.
テキスト3 cha 150: If it is possible, I think you would do well to view the references actively.
テキスト4 cha 158: Later on, it may be of help to /VAR/-sama.

テキスト1 cha 145: I am terribly sorry. Due to a malfunction in this world, it seems that, very rarely, references that should appear much farther ahead can appear.
テキスト2 cha 130: But, hiding them for that reason would be dull, so I shall leave those that have appeared as they are.
テキスト3 cha 150: Shall we call these 'OOPArt references'? OOPArts are objects thought to be entirely out of place in the location or era in which they were discovered.
テキスト4 cha 158: Of course, there is no problem with viewing them, but since they appear because of such a malfunction, their appearance will probably be extremely indistinct.
テキスト5 cha 153: By spending the points you have earned, I believe their clarity will increase somewhat, but I do not think it will be enough for you to see them clearly.
テキスト6 cha 152: Once you reach the scenario in which they should originally be unlocked, you can view them with their usual clarity, so you may wish to wait until then.
テキスト7 cha 102: Well, they should appear much farther ahead, so there is no doubt that they will be an important hint.
